customer-signals.headline: Capture the voice of the
customer-signals.lede: Capture the voice of the customer, identify what matters most, and convert raw conversations into actionable product work inside ServiceNow.

problem.title: Customer needs are trapped in meeting notes, chats, and conversations.
problem.body: Feedback arrives in tickets, surveys, calls, and notes. Nobody sees all of it, the work of turning it into product inputs falls on the people with the least time, and the customer's own words rarely survive the trip to the backlog.
problem.quote: We need a reliable way to capture customer evidence and turn it into prioritized customer needs.

points.title: Needs are buried
points.body: Customer needs sit inside unstructured conversations, spread across calls, notes, spreadsheets, and email.

points.title: Feedback becomes busywork
points.body: Product managers spend as much time entering customer feedback as they do talking to the customer.

points.title: Traceability is lost
points.body: Teams can't follow a shipped feature back to the customer evidence that justified it.

approach.title: Capture signals automatically, then synthesize them into needs.
approach.body: Customer Signals captures, organizes, and makes sense of signals from customers across every interaction. Scattered feedback becomes evidence, evidence becomes prioritized customer needs, and product, service, and platform teams make better-informed decisions about what to build.
before: Product managers spend as much time entering feedback as talking to customers
Customer needs are buried in unstructured conversations
No traceability from customer evidence to shipped features
after: Builders spend their time talking to customers, building, and releasing
Everyone has access to the voice of the customer
Needs are continuously cared for and prioritized, so builders always know what to build next
outcomes: Identify more customer needs, in greater detail
Improve the quality of product inputs
Connect customer evidence to feature development

customer-signals.capabilitiesTitle: Everything between the conversation and the need.

capabilities.title: Customer Signals Agent
capabilities.body: Logs customer conversations and discovers raw signals in them: candidate needs, pain points, feature opportunities, and personas, with the customer's words as evidence.

capabilities.title: Need Designer
capabilities.body: A workbench for pulling signals together to define a new need or strengthen an existing one, and for deduplicating, splitting, and merging needs.

capabilities.title: Need Suggester
capabilities.body: Suggests new needs for older evidence that was never mapped, and existing needs for new evidence as it arrives.

capabilities.title: Customer and persona management
capabilities.body: Define and manage personas, capture them straight from conversations, and see every piece of evidence from a customer in one place.

capabilities.title: Insights
capabilities.body: Automatic nudges about what changed, such as a new need being created or a customer you haven't spoken to in a while.

product-model.headline: Know what is being built,
product-model.lede: Product Model connects customer signals to the complete product definition, from capabilities and features to detailed requirements, while giving product managers a real-time roadmap of what is being built, why it matters, and what comes next.

problem.title: Features get built on assumptions, not customer needs.
problem.body: When the roadmap lives apart from the work and the evidence lives apart from both, every decision needs another review. Stakeholders chase product managers for status, and builders get requirements stripped of the customer statement that motivated them.
problem.quote: We need to understand what is being built, why it matters, and when it will be delivered.

points.title: Assumptions drive the backlog
points.body: Features are defined from opinions and memory instead of the customer needs and evidence behind them.

points.title: Manual translation
points.body: Builders and product managers spend hours turning feedback into product work by hand.

points.title: Strategy and execution drift
points.body: With no real-time connection between the roadmap and the work, decisions slow down and reviews multiply.

approach.title: One structured model, from initiative to requirement.
approach.body: Product Model gives you a structured view of products, initiatives, features, releases, dependencies, and priorities. Teams align stakeholders around priorities, communicate product direction, and adjust plans as customer needs change, moving from raw customer input to release-ready product work.
before: Roadmaps go stale the moment they're shared
Status lives in a product manager's head
Requirements start from a blank page
after: Live roadmaps connected to the work
Everyone sees the same plan and the reason behind it
Requirements generated from features, needs, and evidence
outcomes: Turn customer needs into feature specifications

product-model.capabilitiesTitle: Plan it, specify it, and keep everyone on the same page.

capabilities.title: Roadmap
capabilities.body: Product managers collaborate to build the right things in the right order, based on initiatives from leadership.

capabilities.title: Feature Builder
capabilities.body: Stakeholders and product managers shape features together, with the linked customer needs and evidence in view.

capabilities.title: Connect
capabilities.body: Keeps product managers, leadership, product teams, and internal stakeholders aligned with roadmaps that are connected to the work.

capabilities.title: Inform
capabilities.body: Insights are generated automatically to let people know what is new or noteworthy.

capabilities.title: Requirements Generation Agent
capabilities.body: Generates requirements from feature definitions, customer needs, and customer evidence.

capabilities.title: Build Orchestration Agent
capabilities.body: Takes the generated requirements and supervises the build using ServiceNow Build Agent.

release-intelligence.headline: Release with evidence,
release-intelligence.lede: Improve release quality with phase-gate release management. Connect every release to the customer needs it addresses, close the loop with the customers who asked, and always know the state of a release.

problem.title: Release is an afterthought.
problem.body: Release communication is disconnected from the customer evidence and product decisions behind the work. Customers have to pull release information and hunt for what they care about, and the loop never closes.

points.title: Changes are hard to find
points.body: There's no reliable way to automatically identify what changed in a release.

points.title: The why goes missing
points.body: Release notes say what shipped, but not why it matters or to whom.

points.title: The loop stays open
points.body: Customers and internal users who asked for the work rarely hear that it was delivered.

approach.title: Gate every phase. Connect every release to its reasons.
approach.body: Release Intelligence connects releases to the customer needs, personas, and feature decisions behind them. Releases move through phases only when their gates pass, release notes are generated from the evidence, and the people who asked for the work are told it shipped.
before: Release notes merely tell teams what is shipping
Little rigor or visibility around releases
Writing release notes is a chore that never reaches customers
after: Release scope connects back to the needs, requests, personas, and evidence that justified the work
Phase gates keep quality high and the state of every release visible
Customers hear about the features they care about
outcomes: Show the why behind every release
Turn shipped features into customer value

release-intelligence.capabilitiesTitle: Control the release. Close the loop.

capabilities.title: Phase-gate release management
capabilities.body: Every release follows the phases you define. Gates check conditions before a release can advance, and only release managers can promote a phase or override a failed gate, with a recorded reason.

capabilities.title: Release Workbench
capabilities.body: One view of a release: the current phase, days left, the latest gate results, a timeline of phases and milestones, and the release notes.

capabilities.title: Release Calendar
capabilities.body: Phases and milestones for every active release on one calendar, filtered to the releases you care about.

capabilities.title: Release Notes Agent
capabilities.body: Connects release scope back to the customer needs, feature requests, personas, and evidence behind it, and writes release notes from them.

capabilities.title: Release Manager Agent
capabilities.body: Tracks phase gates and release state, and flags a release in jeopardy before it slips.
